bg-13-01.hint: The room is spacious and clean.
bg-13-01.why: Attach -고 directly to adjective stem 넓- → 넓고.

bg-13-01.q: Connect two sequential actions: eating a meal and drinking coffee. Use 먹다 + -고 and 마시다 in the past tense (-았/었어요).
bg-13-01.why: In past-tense sentences with -고, only the final verb takes the past ending.

steps.en: The room is spacious and clean.
My room is spacious and clean.

en: On weekends, I usually clean the house.
I do the cleaning and do the laundry.
And I listen to music and rest comfortably.

bg-13-01.q: What does the person do after cleaning?
bg-13-01.why: The passage says '청소를 하고 빨래를 해요' (I clean and do laundry).
The passage says '음악을 듣고 편하게 쉬어요' (I listen to music and rest comfortably).

items: Connect actions and descriptions smoothly using -고
Remember to place past tense markers only on the final verb

bg-13-02.why: Attach -지만 directly to adjective stem 어렵- → 어렵지만.

bg-13-02.q: Contrast the price and taste of a dish (expensive but delicious). Use 비싸다 + -지만 and 맛있다 in the polite present (-아요/어요).
bg-13-02.why: Attach -지만 directly to stem 비싸- to contrast two qualities.

steps.en: The food is spicy, but delicious.
Korean food is spicy, but delicious.

en: The food at this restaurant is expensive.
However, the food is really delicious.
The shop is small, but there are always many customers.

bg-13-02.q: What is true about the restaurant's food?
bg-13-02.why: The text states '음식 값이 비싸요. 그렇지만 음식이 정말 맛있어요' (It is expensive, but really delicious).

bg-13-02.q: What is characteristic of the shop itself?
options: It is small but has many customers
It is very large and empty
bg-13-02.why: The passage says '가게는 작지만 손님이 항상 많아요' (The shop is small, but there are always many customers).

items: Express contrast between two clauses using -지만
Attach -지만 directly to adjective and verb stems without vowel harmony changes

bg-13-03.hint: Outside is cold, but inside the room is warm.
bg-13-03.why: -지만 attaches directly to the regular stem: 춥- + -지만 → 춥지만.

bg-13-03.q: Connect listening to music and reading a newspaper in the morning. Use 듣다 + -고 and 읽다 in the polite present (-아요/어요).
bg-13-03.why: 듣다 attaches -고 directly to base stem 듣- without changing ㄷ to ㄹ.

bg-13-03.hint: Before consonant endings like -고, ㄷ irregular verbs retain their base stem: 듣- + -고 → 듣고.
bg-13-03.why: ㄷ changes to ㄹ only before vowels; before consonant endings like -고, it stays 듣고.

steps.en: Outside is cold, but the room is warm.
Outside is cold, but our room is warm.

ko: 저는 따뜻한 차를 마시고 책을 읽어요.
en: The weather is cold, but the sky is clear.
I drink warm tea and read a book.

bg-13-03.why: The text states '날씨는 춥지만 하늘은 맑아요' (The weather is cold, but the sky is clear).

bg-13-03.q: What is the writer doing inside?
options: Drinking warm tea and reading a book
bg-13-03.why: The text states '따뜻한 차를 마시고 책을 읽어요' (I drink warm tea and read a book).

items: Attach -고 and -지만 directly to irregular verb stems without unnecessary sound shifts
Keep the base stems of ㄷ and ㅂ verbs intact when attaching consonant endings

bg-13-04.hint: The library is quiet and cool.
bg-13-04.why: Listing two positive traits in the same direction calls for -고.

bg-13-04.q: Contrast someone being busy with always being kind. Use 바쁘다 + -지만 and 친절하다 in the polite present (-아요/어요).
bg-13-04.why: -지만 connects two contrasting ideas: being busy vs being kind.

bg-13-04.hint: Quiet and cool are harmonious positive traits, so connect them with -고 rather than contrasting -지만.
bg-13-04.why: When two clauses point in the same positive direction, use connection -고, not contrast -지만.

steps.en: The library is quiet and cool.
Our school library is quiet and cool.

ko: 제 친구 수진이는 성격이 밝고 친절해요.
요즘 시험 준비 때문에 바쁘지만 항상 웃어요.
우리는 같이 도서관에서 책을 읽고 공부해요.
en: My friend Sujin is bright and kind.
She is busy preparing for exams these days, but she always smiles.
We read books and study together at the library.

bg-13-04.why: The text states '수진이는 성격이 밝고 친절해요' (Sujin is bright and kind).

bg-13-04.q: What does Sujin do even though she is busy with exam preparations?
options: She takes a break from school
bg-13-04.why: The text says '바쁘지만 항상 웃어요' (She is busy, but she always smiles).

items: Choose appropriately between -고 for sequential/harmonious traits and -지만 for contrasts
Construct multi-clause compound sentences expressing both addition and contrast
